messages:
Lena Park: Quick idea from the perf spike last night: introduce a short-lived 'fast-path' microqueue per-tenant to absorb microbursts (<=150 reqs) without blowing up coalesce windows. notes below.

Lena Park: motivation: continuous batcher tries to maximize KV reuse and batching but small bursts force window growth and hurt tail latency. we need something that preserves cache locality while giving fast service to tiny interactive flows.

Tomas Nguyen: sounds promising. how is this different from the 'burst lanes' prototypes we've seen?

Lena Park: key differences: 1) microqueues are ephemeral FIFO queues that live for max 200ms, 2) they borrow admission credits instead of stealing global concurrency, 3) they have a soft admission token that is charged only on dequeue (so enqueue is cheap). they also prefer local KV hot slices.

Priya Iyer: operational Qs: how do we avoid per-tenant state explosion? if many tenants idle but each has a microqueue, that's bad.

Lena Park: we only allocate the microqueue structure lazily on burst detection and garbage-collect after idle_ms threshold. the state is tiny (pointer+credit). also there's a global cap of active microqueues per-GPU.

Ana Soto: this will change KV cache hit patterns. do you have simulated cache hit deltas?

Lena Park: ran a sim with 10k tenant mix (80% small, 20% large). KV hit-rate for shared shards dipped 0.9% during bursts; end-to-end p99 for interactive flows improved ~95ms. overall p50 unchanged. detailed numbers:

```
experiment:
  microqueue:
    enabled: true
    max_life_ms: 200
    max_req: 150
    enqueue_ttl_ms: 50
    token_charge_on_dequeue: true
    per_tenant_initial_credits: 40
    global_active_microqueues_limit: 256
    idle_gc_ms: 5000
admission:
  borrow_from_global_pool: true
  borrow_threshold_pct: 20
metrics:
  emit: [microqueue_active, microqueue_demotions, microqueue_shedding]
```

Priya Iyer: what about fairness if a tenant continuously bursts and never cools down?

Lena Park: two mitigations: (a) demotion window: if a tenant triggers microqueue > N times in M seconds, they are rate-limited into coalescing for a cooldown period; (b) credit decay: sustained bursting drains their per-tenant credits faster than refill.

Tomas Nguyen: failure modes: if microqueues saturate the GPU, do we block the main batcher or do we preempt? my preference: preempt microqueues or shed low-value fast requests first.

Lena Park: agreed — default behavior is to preempt microqueues when global free slots < 10% and to start shedding non-interactive low-priority microrequests per policy. we have a config toggle to invert that for premium-only nodes.

Ana Soto: add KV affinity label to microqueue entries so we can favor ones likely to hit the cache. also log per-shard hit/miss during microqueue windows so evaluators can measure regression.

Observability-bot: checklist: add these telemetry points -> microqueue_alloc, microqueue_eviction_reason, microqueue_serialize_delay, per_tenant_microqueue_hits. create alert if microqueue_eviction_reason == "GC" > 2% over 10m.

Priya Iyer: rollout plan? we should A/B on a small subset of GPUs and turn on strict quotas for demo tenants to avoid gaming.

Lena Park: will stage to eng-runtime/stage with 2% sample of traffic, 72h A/B, metrics: p99 interactive, per-tenant demotions, KV hit delta, and cost delta. tagging @ana for dashboard changes and @tomas for preemption hooks.

Tomas Nguyen: one more ask: add a deterministic fallback for requests that require strict ordering (we can't reorder some seq APIs into microqueues). label those as "order_sensitive=false/true" and bypass microqueue if true.

Lena Park: good catch. will add ordering bit to request envelope and honor it in admission. posting experimental results at end of A/B. :wave:
